metadata.title: [CHORE]: Plugin bindings payload hardening — restrict caller-overridable config keys
metadata.author: gandhipratik203

description:
### 📝 Summary

`POST /v1/tools/plugin_bindings` currently accepts a free-form `config: Dict[str, Any]` per policy. Any key the caller sends is stored verbatim and merged into the per-tenant plugin config at runtime. There's no distinction between config that belongs at the gateway/operator layer and config that's genuinely meant to be set per (team, tool, plugin) by the caller.

This works, but it leaves the binding API with a wider responsibility than it really needs. Worth tightening.

### 🤔 Background

The binding API was introduced in #4068 with typed Pydantic schemas per plugin — each plugin had a known set of fields.

#4286 removed those per-plugin schemas, for sound architectural reasons: plugin contracts live in `cpex-plugins`, not in CF, so CF shouldn't have to know which plugins exist or what their config shape is. After that change, `config` became a fully open `Dict[str, Any]` that CF persists verbatim.

The decoupling intent was right. The side effect is that the API stopped distinguishing between two layers of plugin config that used to be implicitly separated:

- **Operator layer** — set once on the gateway and increasingly inherited from env (see #4582). Not meaningful per-tenant; the same value applies fleet-wide.
- **Caller layer** — behaviour knobs that legitimately vary per (team, tool). The whole reason the binding API exists.

Today both flow through the same opaque `config` dict, with no enforcement of which keys belong to which layer.

### 📐 Possible directions (open for discussion)

A couple of shapes that have come up — happy to defer to whatever the team prefers:

1. **Restrict the binding payload to caller-layer keys only.** Operator-layer keys come from the gateway-side plugin YAML (which already supports env substitution per #4582) and aren't accepted through the API.
2. **Plugin-declared allowlist.** Each plugin's gateway-side YAML declares which keys are caller-overridable; the binding API filters incoming payloads against that declared list. Keeps CF generic — the contract sits with the plugin author, where #4286 wanted it.

(1) and (2) compose well; (2) is the mechanism for (1). Either way, the goal is to put the layer boundary back in place without re-coupling CF to plugin-specific schemas.

### 🛟 Existing data

Any rows written under the current contract may contain keys that the tighter contract wouldn't accept. Worth a review pass once the new shape is decided.

### 📓 Related

- #4068 — introduced the binding API with typed per-plugin config schemas
- #4286 — removed the per-plugin schemas (correct decoupling; this issue is the natural follow-up)
- #4582 — operator-side env inheritance for plugin config; complements this work
